chunks: My father narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated from Ali b. Ma'bad from al-Husayn b. Khalid from Ali b. Musa al-Rida from his father from his forefathers from Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon them.

He said: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever does not believe in my Pond, Allah will not direct him to my Pond. Whoever does not believe in my intercession, I will not intercede to Allah for him. Then he said: Surely, my intercession is for those of my Nation who have committed major sins. As for the pious, they will have no need for it. Al-Husayn b. Khalid said: So I said to al-Rida: O son of the Messenger of Allah! What is the meaning of Allah's saying 'They do not intercede except for whom He approves'? He said: They will not intercede except for those whose religion Allah approves of.

key_terms.الكبائر: al-kaba'ir - major sins, the primary beneficiaries of intercession
key_terms.حوض: al-Hawd - the Pond of the Prophet, a station on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.شفاعة: shafa'a - intercession, the Prophet's advocacy for sinners before God

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about the Prophet's intercession for sinners?
ai.summary: A hadith from the Prophet transmitted through Imam al-Rida from his forefathers from Imam Ali, declaring that whoever denies the Pond will not reach it, and whoever denies intercession will not receive it. The Prophet clarifies that his intercession is specifically for those of his community who commit major sins, while the pious have no need for it. Al-Husayn b. Khalid then asks Imam al-Rida about the Quranic verse 'They do not intercede except for whom He approves' (21:28), and the Imam explains it means only those whose religion Allah approves of will be interceded for. This teaching was delivered in the context of seventh-century Rajab gatherings where eschatological topics were especially relevant.
